document_title: Hikrobot 'Mobile Robot Product Catalog', full version, English, 69 pages. Document code 'R.101.EN.26Q2.1' (p.69), file name states 2026 Q2 V1, updated 16 Jun 2026.
researcher_notes:
SCOPE: this is the second of the two files that had never been extracted by any prior pass. It was deferred across 4+ consecutive sessions purely on size grounds and had never been opened. It is the single largest yield of the whole corpus: 15 separate specification tables covering 73 distinct model numbers across 11 product families, against a DB that currently holds 10 Hikrobot products. 69 of the 73 are new; only 4 match an existing DB row.

METHOD: I built a page map first (one line per page: character count + first four lines) rather than reading linearly, which located all 15 spec tables in a single pass and showed that pp.1-17 and pp.51-69 are marketing/case-study content with no vehicle specifications. Every spec table then extracted cleanly as text via pdfplumber — unlike the VisionNav catalog, NO page of this document needed rendering. Total: the technical content of a 69-page catalog lives on 15 pages.

*** THE FOUR DB MATCHES, AND WHY ONE OF THEM IS A NAMING PROBLEM RATHER THAN A DATA PROBLEM ***
- Hikrobot Q7-1000E (p.18): max_payload 1000 and max_speed 2.0 both CONFIRMED exactly. Clean enrich.
- Hikrobot F3-1500 (p.24): three conflicts (max_speed 2.1 vs 1.5, min_aisle_width 2100 vs 2213, vehicle_width 870 vs 863) but vehicle_length, lifting_height, stop_accuracy, drive_type and stacking_capability all confirmed exactly. Note that the sibling F3-1000 IS rated 2.0 m/s, so the stored 2.1 may be a mis-attributed sibling value.
- Hikrobot F5-1600 (p.26): DB max_payload 1600 vs the table's 1350. The MODEL NAME says 1600 and the SPEC TABLE says 1350. This is the identical failure mode found the same day in VisionNav's VNP20 (name implies 2000, table says 1900) — a payload read off a model number rather than a spec row. It is now a documented cross-supplier error class, and it matters because max_payload is KO_IF_LT: an overstated value wins tenders the truck cannot serve.
- Hikrobot F4-1000C (p.22): SIX values disagree at once (lifting_height, min_aisle_width, max_speed, stop_accuracy, vehicle_length, vehicle_width) while max_payload and charge_time agree. Six simultaneous disagreements is not the shape of a data-entry error, it is the shape of two different machines — and the catalog's model is named 'F4-1000', without the DB's 'C' suffix. Filed as a conflict, but the first question to answer is a naming question, not a value question.

*** PARTIAL COVERAGE: 6 of the 10 existing DB products are NOT in this catalog. ***
F1-1000U-A, F1-300T-A, Q2L-300A, Q3-600C, Q7-1000D and Q7-1500D have no page here. In three cases the catalog carries a SIBLING with a different suffix (Q2-400D vs Q2L-300A; Q3-600D/Q3S-600A vs Q3-600C; Q7-1000E/Q7-1500E vs Q7-1000D/Q7-1500D). Per this project's convention those are candidates for review as possibly-superseded models — but this agent only flags; nothing is deactivated or deleted.

*** THE ONE THING TO DECIDE BEFORE IMPORTING ANY OF THIS: how much of this catalog is actually in AP0's scope? ***
AP0's product_type has exactly three values (Forklift AGV / Tugger AGV / Mobile AMR), and Hikrobot's range does not partition cleanly into them:
- The TP6 STU series (5 models, p.37) are 12-metre-tall, aisle-bound, BUSBAR-POWERED tote robots. They are closer to an ASRS shuttle than to a free-roaming AMR — the catalog itself says they are 'actively replacing traditional Miniload/palletizer systems'. I typed them Mobile AMR because nothing else fits, but a reasonable Tech Lead decision is that they are not Products in this database at all.
- The CH cantilever robots (3 models, p.43) handle reels and spools on a cantilever arm. AP0's load_type list has no allowed value for a reel, roll or spool, so load_type is NULL on all three.
- The CT series (4 models, p.41) are latent tow tractors: they drive UNDER a cart (260-320 mm tall) and lift a traction pin into it. I typed them Tugger AGV on the strength of 'Conveying type: Traction', but CT7L-1000 has no traction pin at all (both pin rows read '/'), so that one model's classification is genuinely uncertain.
I have flagged rather than guessed everywhere this bit. 73 products is a large claim against a 10-product incumbent and the scoping decision should be made deliberately.

*** SYSTEMATIC EXTRACTION DECISIONS APPLIED THROUGHOUT (stated once here, cited per product) ***
1. UNITS. Every speed row in this catalog is printed in mm/s and AP0's unit is m/s — 73 conversions. Every charge-time row is printed in HOURS and AP0's unit is MINUTES — another 68 conversions. An unconverted value here would be off by 1000x or 60x on fields that feed scoring. Both the printed and converted figures are in every citation.
2. charge_time is safe here — it is an absolute duration, not one of the four known traps (not a ratio, not a partial 20-80% charge, not a current in amperes, not a C-rate). Where the source prints a range ('2~3 h') the conservative upper bound is used; where it prints a ceiling ('<=2 h') that ceiling is used.
3. max_speed is taken from 'Rated running speed (EMPTY)', which is exactly the unloaded/top figure AP0's hint asks for. This catalog never prints a loaded/unloaded pair, so the dual-figure trap does not arise. Two exceptions are flagged: F6-2000's row is mislabelled '(mm/s)' while printing a m/s value, and the TP6 marketing page claims 3.5 m/s against the table's 3000 mm/s (table used).
4. battery_runtime: every family prints '6~8 h'. AP0's hint states no direction, so the conservative lower bound 6 is used and the range is in the citation. The HC family (p.47) is the sole exception — it prints a flat '8', so 8 is used unreduced.
5. min_ground_clearance holds the ROBOT HEIGHT, not the chassis gap — the field name is a known trap and the AP0 hint says 'Source: vehicle height spec'. This matters unusually much here because SEVEN of these spec tables print an actual row called 'Chassis ground clearance' (15-40 mm) sitting right next to the dimension row. Taking that row would have put a 20-40 mm value into a K.O. field that should hold 250-2750 mm. It is deliberately left unmapped; it has no AP0 field.
6. rotation_capable is left NULL on all 73 products, even though five tables carry a 'Rotation capacity: 360 degrees in-place rotation' row. That row is the VEHICLE spinning; AP0's rotation_capable means rotating the CARRIED RACK to present a face. This is the documented mis-mapping that has already corrupted rows at two other suppliers. The holonomic capability is recorded in omnidirectional_movement instead. Note the DB already holds rotation_capable=1 on five Hikrobot LMR rows — not contradicted by this document, but not supported either.
7. 'Rotation diameter' rows (in 8 of the 15 tables) are DIAMETERS and are never mapped to min_turning_radius, per the established rule. The one exception is the CT series, whose row is explicitly labelled 'Arc turning RADIUS' — those four are mapped to the Tugger-scope turning_radius field.

NOTHING WAS WRITTEN TO AIRTABLE. No existing non-null DB value is proposed for overwrite anywhere in this file.

company_wide_context.notes:
service_coverage: p.3 states 'Business covers 50+ countries, with branches founded in the Netherlands, France, Germany, Hungary, Korea, Japan, Singapore, and Malaysia'. That yields four unambiguous EU ISO codes (NL, FR, DE, HU) but the DB currently holds the single value 'EU' on every Hikrobot product row. I have NOT proposed a change, because 'branches founded in' is a sales/branch statement, not a service-network guarantee, and narrowing 'EU' to four countries could wrongly disqualify the supplier. Flagged for a decision.

fleet_management_system: NOT mapped. The DB holds the non-conforming string 'Proprietary (RCS 2000)' on two rows (allowed values are Proprietary / Open API / VDA 5050 compatible / Third-party WMS native). This catalog never names 'RCS 2000' at all — p.7 and p.13 describe the scheduling layer generically, and p.4 dates 'Released RCS and iWMS' to 2016. The recurring AP0 limitation applies: RCS is a proprietary product that is also explicitly open ('fully open to developers', 'support secondary development'), and the single-select cannot express both.

vda5050_compatible: NOT mapped. The string 'VDA 5050' does not appear anywhere in these 69 pages. The DB holds vda5050_compatible=1 for Hikrobot Q3-600C. This document neither supports nor contradicts that; per the field's NULL RULE, silence is not evidence.

functional_safety_level: NOT mapped, and this is a real loss. p.4 states 'Got SIL & CE Certification: AMR Integrated Safety Controller' — but 'SIL' is given with NO level number, and AP0's allowed values are None/PLd/PLe/SIL 2/SIL 3. An unnumbered SIL claim cannot be stored. p.16 adds 'Our AMR adopts fully independent safety assemblies'.

reference_count: NOT mapped. p.4 gives '100,000 AMRs produced as of May, 2024', '50,000+ AMRs delivered', 'Over 1,500 AMR customers worldwide' and 'Ranked top in global shipments for 3 consecutive years (from Interact Analysis)'. These are unit-shipment and customer counts, not completed reference installs, and the AP0 hint asks specifically for install references. Recording 100,000 would be a category error. Worth noting that AP0 has no field for installed-base or market-share evidence at all, which is the strongest commercial signal this document contains.

max_fleet_size: NOT mapped — no number is published. p.13 claims 'clustering scheduling' and p.14 describes multi-AMR warehouse paradigms, but no fleet ceiling is stated.

IBASE (p.16-17) is Hikrobot's fourth-generation AMR architecture platform ('1+N+X: Based on one intelligent base, Hikrobot derives N types of AMRs, covering X scenarios'). It is a genuine shared-platform statement across the whole range and is exactly the kind of thing the Base Model layer exists for — but it is a hardware ARCHITECTURE shared across families, not a single base model, so it cannot be expressed as one base_model_id. Worth a note when the import script author decides base-model grouping.

distribution_model: NOT mapped. p.3 describes a domestic branch/office/service network and overseas branches; p.4 mentions an 'Eco-Partner 3.0 Program'. That is consistent with both Direct and Dealer Network and the document does not disambiguate.

AP0's load_type list has no allowed value for a reel/roll/spool, so load_type is left NULL. top_module_type='Custom' is the closest fit.
